newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to decide on IMF loan drawdown by July 31.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to decide on IMF loan drawdown by July 31.

text.p: Bulgaria is expected to decide by July 31 whether to draw down immediately a $130 million loan extended by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) under an IMF standby agreement, Prime Minister Ivan Kostov said on Thursday.
He told reporters the Monetary Policy Council would make the decision on the basis of the country's balance of payments.
The IMF on Wednesday approved the release of a $130 million instalment of $510 standby credit agreed in April.
After the tranche is drawn down it becomes a liability of the central bank's banking department which should be balanced by an increase of government debt managed by the department.
Bulgaria may receive the next IMF tranche without further review of the country's structural reforms, Kostov said.

The Monetary Policy Council is expected to decide by the end of the month whether Bulgaria should offer a short-term bridge financing scheme by placing pools of Bulgarian enterprises as collateral with foreign investment banks, he said.

Kostov said it was important to consolidate the administration of the country's foreign debt at the finance ministry. The Council for Economic Development at the presidency on Wednesday discussed the idea of setting up a consolidated register of the debt at the finance ministry.

Deputy Finance Minister Plamen Oresharski said on Wednesday the register was expected to be set up by the end of July and the finance ministry would take over the full management of Bulgaria's foreign debt.
At present some of Bulgaria's foreign debt is part of the balance sheet of Bulbank, Bulgaria's biggest state bank.
"Clarifying the relations between Bulbank and the Finance Ministry will help the restructuring of Bulbank into a universal commercial bank and its future privatisation," Kostov said.
